name: KC-46 Pegasus
summary: Twin-engine aerial refueling tanker and cargo aircraft based on the Boeing 767, replacing the KC-135 in USAF service.

wings: Low-mounted swept wing with no winglets
Hose-and-drogue refueling pods under each outer wing
engines: Two large high-bypass turbofans on pylons under the wing
fuselage: Wide twin-aisle-size fuselage in grey with only a few windows near the front
Large cargo door on the forward left side
Refueling boom under the tail plus a centerline drogue unit

tellTales: Twin-engine widebody with a refueling boom under the tail
Hose-drogue pods under each outer wing
Grey widebody with only a handful of windows near the front

confusedWith.howToTell: The KC-46 is grey with a refueling boom, wing refueling pods and almost no windows; a 767 airliner has full rows of cabin windows and no boom.
The KC-46 has two big engines on a wide fuselage; the KC-135 has four engines on a narrow fuselage.

usCount.source: Boeing KC-46 delivery reports (105th delivered April 2026) / Air & Space Forces Magazine
